production.note: US model years. Sedan 2009 to 2014: GM introduced the "2009 Cadillac CTS-V", and GM Media published a 2014 CTS-V Sedan specification table (source gm-2014-ctsv-sedan-specs). Coupe 2011 to 2015: GM's release "Art And Science: Cadillac Premieres 2011 CTS-V Coupe" (source gm-2011-ctsv-coupe-release); Consumer Guide, May 2014, quotes Cadillac announcing "production of a limited, special-edition 2015 CTS-V Coupe, marking the last chapter of the current model before the next generation of the V-Series debuts next year", 500 cars (source consumerguide-ctsv-2015). Wagon 2011 to 2014: first appears in GM Media's 2011 material (source gm-2011-ctsv-wagon-features) and last in the 2014 product information (source gm-2014-ctsv-wagon-info).

body.note: Sedan: "4-door sport luxury sedan, RWD". Coupe from the 2011 model year (source gm-2011-ctsv-coupe-release). Wagon (CTS-V Sport Wagon) from the 2011 model year (source gm-2011-ctsv-wagon-features). All three share the 556 hp engine and both transmissions.

transmission.note: GM table: "six-speed manual (Tremec TR6060); six-speed automatic (Hydra-Matic 6L90)". Both from launch: GM's 2009 release names "a new, Tremec TR6060 six-speed manual with a dual-disc clutch; and a Hydra-Matic 6L90 six-speed automatic" (source gm-2009-ctsv-release). The coupe and wagon were offered with the same two gearboxes (sources gm-2011-ctsv-coupe-release, gm-2014-ctsv-wagon-info).

powerHp.note: Quote, GM Media release for the 2009 CTS-V: "Rated at 556 horsepower (415 kW) and 551 lb.-ft. of torque (747 Nm)". GM Media's 2012 sedan table: "Horsepower (hp / kW @ rpm): 556 / 415 @ 6100*" with the footnote "*SAE certified." (source gm-2012-ctsv-sedan-specs); the 2014 table repeats it (source gm-2014-ctsv-sedan-specs), so the rating was unchanged for the whole run. GM's preliminary 2009 material estimated 550 hp (see discrepancies).

weightLb.note: Manufacturer curb weight, sedan with the six-speed manual, 2010 model year. Quote, GM's 2010 CTS-V specification table: "Curb weight, manual, lbs. (kg): 4222 (1915)"; the automatic is "4255 (1930)". GM Media's 2012 table gives the same: "Curb weight (lb / kg): 4222 / 1915 (manual) 4255 / 1930 (automatic)" (source gm-2012-ctsv-sedan-specs). GM's preliminary 2009 table had only estimates, "manual: 4200 / 1905 (est)" (source gm-2009-ctsv-prelim-specs), so the reference model year is 2010, the first with a final figure; the power rating is the same for every model year. The 2014 table gives 4219 / 1914 (source gm-2014-ctsv-sedan-specs). See discrepancies.

discrepancies.reason: Estimate vs final rating: GM's preliminary 2009 table gave "550 / 410 @ 6200 (est)" before SAE certification; the production rating is 556 hp at 6,100 rpm.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 556 hp, the rating in GM's 2009 release and marked SAE certified in GM Media's 2012 and 2014 tables.

discrepancies.reason: Estimate and model year: 4,200 lb is GM's pre-production estimate for the 2009 manual sedan ("est"); 4,222 lb is the manual sedan in GM's 2010 and 2012 tables; 4,219 lb is the same row in the 2014 table.
discrepancies.resolution: Used 4,222 lb, the earliest non-estimated manufacturer figure for the manual sedan (2010 model year, repeated for 2012).
